fixes.explanation: Paul doesn't give us that option. Staying clear of someone isn't bearing with them. Keeping your distance is easier, I'll admit it, but that isn't what verse 1 says. He says the strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak.

Paul says the opposite. The verse says the strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak “…and not to please ourselves.” So the strong don't get to put themselves first. The whole verse points the other way, toward bearing with the shortcomings of the weak.
Paul doesn't say that. Winning someone over isn't in the verse. What he says is to please your neighbor for his good, to build him up. The aim is his good.

Paul says everything written in the past was written for our instruction. So those old words are there to teach us. I read a recipe so I can bake the thing, not so I can frame the page. Paul goes on to say that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

Seeking is a good thing to do, baker, but it isn't Paul's word in this verse. He says the harmony is so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify “…the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.” One mind and one voice means they do it together, not each one off in a corner. That's a choir, not a bunch of solo acts.

Paul says the opposite, baker. He says to accept one another, just as Christ accepted you, “…in order to bring glory to God.” So when you accept somebody, glory goes to God. That's a big result for something as simple as making room for someone.
That's a nice picture, but it's not what Isaiah says. The words are “in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.” It's about hope, not a home. Hope is the word Paul lands on here.

Keeping the law isn't in Isaiah's words, friend. They say “in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.” Notice where the hope rests: in Him, the Root of Jesse. Paul lines up one verse after another about the Gentiles, and this last one lands on Him.
Paul says you may overflow with hope “…by the power of the Holy Spirit.” The power behind the overflow is the Spirit's. And friend, overflow is the word, like a cookie jar nobody can close.

Elders aren't named in this verse, baker. Paul says you may overflow with hope “…by the power of the Holy Spirit.” Overflow is a big word, so Paul points to a big source. The Holy Spirit is the power he names.
